entry.title: Research Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: Research coverage this week is anchored by the Hermes-Claude subscription integration: a deep-dive on the pipeline architecture that lets Hermes drive the unmodified official Claude Code CLI, paired with a security-focused guide to its keyless authentication flow — both directly actionable for users running or evaluating the plugin. Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (released 21 September 2026) adds a --format stream-json flag emitting structured JSONL, an immediate upgrade win for anyone scripting against the CLI. The broader agent ecosystem rounds out the section: AgentProto v0.20.0 (22 September 2026) is a new open-source runtime that already lists Hermes among its integrated agents, worth tracking for interoperability, while Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 hardens MCP security with per-invocation session scoping — a pattern relevant to Hermes's own MCP discovery and integration configuration.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Deep-dive on the pipeline powering the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: Hermes talks to a plugin that drives the unmodified official Claude Code executable, with conversation flowing as native stream-json while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, approvals and compaction. No forked CLI or patched binary is used. Every request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools and skills disabled so Hermes controls the tool inventory. An admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request per turn, rejecting native retry attempts locally to keep billing honest. Version requirements: Hermes 0.21.4+ and the qualified native Claude Code 2.1.263.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Covers Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (tagged v2026.9.21, released 21 September 2026), which adds a --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL, one JSON object per line, enabling reliable parsing by scripts and pipelines. Upgrade paths include hermes update for git installs, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The same release rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency. The feature is free and built into the open-source agent.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Explains authentication for the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: credentials remain entirely with the official Claude Code CLI via a one-time claude auth login flow; the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes or prints credential files, and no API key is required or sent anywhere in the flow. The plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint and cloud override variables, naming conflicting variables without exposing their values. Status checks like claude auth status read the local credential store locally in roughly 0.3s. Separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR to point at a dedicated CLI-managed config directory.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Review of AgentProto, an open-source agentic runtime in TypeScript released as v0.20.0 on 22 September 2026. It provides one interface to start, message, watch and stop coding agents in the background with quality gates before work lands. Its README claims integration with 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode and Mastra. The project is Apache-2.0 licensed and free, with users paying only for underlying model usage. The reviewer notes it is very early: single-digit GitHub stars, alpha-level Tier 2 components, and a verdict of interesting architecture but early-adopters-only.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Overview of Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, tagged on GitHub on 18 September 2026. Key changes center on MCP security: sessions are scoped per invocation with requests authenticated against the correct invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives are now ZIP-only with digest verification, and ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected. New vector-store connectors were added for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB and Azure Cosmos DB, plus in-memory and portable filters. The article flags breaking changes, including deprecation of the MCP sampling callback, and warns readers to review before upgrading.
